data.name: Australian Pikelets With Butter And Jam
data.description: These small, golden griddle pancakes have soft, fluffy centres and a gently sweet flavour. A spread of butter melts into their warm surfaces, while strawberry jam adds a bright, fruity finish.

not_suitable_for: People with wheat allergy or coeliac disease

refrigerator.notes: Store plain pikelets separately from the toppings. Cool briefly on a wire rack, then refrigerate in an airtight container within 2 hours, or within 1 hour when the ambient temperature exceeds 32°C (90°F). Keep at 4°C (40°F) or below.

freezer.notes: Freeze cooled, plain pikelets in an airtight container with parchment between layers. Thaw in the refrigerator.

storage.reheating: Microwave plain pikelets on a microwave-safe plate in short bursts until the centre reaches 74°C (165°F). Add butter and jam after reheating.

items.name: egg
items.notes: Weigh without the shell; approximately 1 large egg.

items.name: unsalted butter
items.notes: Divide into four 3 g portions for greasing the pan between batches.

instructions.text: Weigh all ingredients, keeping the butter for the pan separate from the serving butter.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt together in the large mixing bowl until evenly distributed.
Whisk the milk and egg together in the mixing jug until no streaks of egg remain.
Fold the milk mixture into the dry ingredients with the flexible spatula, stopping as soon as no dry flour remains. The batter should fall from the spatula in thick ribbons; small lumps are fine.

doneness_cues.visual: Thick, spoonable batter with no pockets of dry flour.

instructions.text: Rest the batter for 5 minutes to hydrate the flour.
Preheat the large nonstick frying pan over medium-low heat for about 2 minutes.

Cook four batches of four pikelets, using 3 g of the pan butter per batch. Spoon approximately 25 g batter per pikelet into the buttered pan, leaving room for each to spread to about 6–7 cm across. Cook for 1½–2 minutes until bubbles open on top and the edges look set, then turn with the thin turner and cook for about 1 minute more. Each pikelet should be golden on both sides with a set centre reaching at least 71°C (160°F), checked by inserting the fine-tip thermometer horizontally into the thickest part. Allow about 12 minutes for all four batches.

doneness_cues.visual: Golden surfaces, set edges and a centre without wet batter.
doneness_cues.tactile: The centre springs back gently when lightly pressed.

tips: Reduce the heat if the underside browns before bubbles appear on top.
Do not press the pikelets down after turning.

instructions.text: Serve the warm pikelets on the serving plate with the softened butter and strawberry jam, dividing the toppings evenly.

troubleshooting.symptom: The pikelets are dark underneath but wet in the middle.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The pan is too hot or the batter portions are too large.
troubleshooting.prevention: Use medium-low heat and approximately 25 g batter per pikelet.
troubleshooting.fix: Lower the heat and continue cooking, turning as needed, until the centres are set and reach 71°C (160°F). Severely burnt surfaces cannot be fixed.

troubleshooting.symptom: The pikelets are dense or rubbery.
troubleshooting.likely_cause: The batter was mixed excessively or the baking powder has lost its strength.
troubleshooting.prevention: Use fresh baking powder and stop folding as soon as the dry flour disappears.
troubleshooting.fix: The cooked texture cannot be reversed; serve warm with the butter and jam.

chef_notes: Keep portions small and consistent so the centres cook before the surfaces become too dark.
A few small batter lumps are preferable to prolonged mixing, which develops gluten and toughens the crumb.
Butter should foam gently in the pan. If it quickly turns dark, reduce the heat before adding batter.

Use a clean thermometer probe to check the centre: egg dishes should reach 71°C (160°F), and reheated leftovers should reach 74°C (165°F). [FoodSafety.gov minimum temperatures](https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/safe-minimum-internal-temperatures).
data.cultural_context: In Australia, pikelets are small, fluffy pancakes enjoyed as snacks, lunchbox treats and at breakfast. Their compact size and affinity for sweet toppings distinguish this familiar style of griddle pancake. [Australian pikelet reference](https://www.coles.com.au/recipes-inspiration/recipes/pikelet-recipe).
